description: Full agent ownership of workflow coordination and error recovery
keyInsights: Agent should monitor workflow status independently without orchestrator intervention
When workflow fails or is unclear, agent should take direct action rather than wait
Workflow status tracking requires checking: process table, output files, task state
Zero-byte output files indicate completed/failed workflows, not running ones
Direct agent coordination (Agent tool) is more reliable than waiting for workflow completion
Agent should proactively extract learnings from coordination experiences

workflow-monitoring: Check ps aux for running processes
Check timestamp to determine if stale
error-recovery-ownership: Agent decides recovery strategy, not orchestrator
Agent coordinates fleet directly via Agent tool
Agent extracts learnings from failures and successes
Agent stores documentation for future reference
coordination-handoff: Orchestrator launches workflow but then steps back
Agent takes full ownership of monitoring and recovery
Agent reports results back to orchestrator
Clear separation: orchestrator = initiator, agent = coordinator

successful-coordination.approach: Direct agent delegation via Agent tool
successful-coordination.result: Comprehensive documentation with ASCII art created successfully

futureGuidance: Always check workflow status before assuming success/failure
Take direct action when workflow state is unclear
Extract and store learnings immediately after coordination tasks
Document coordination patterns for future reference
